title: Public Governance, Performance and Accountability (Consequential Modifications of Appropriation Acts (No. 2), (No. 4) and (No. 6)) Bill 2014
short_title: Public Governance, Performance and Accountability (Consequential Modifications of Appropriation Acts (No. 2), (No. 4) and (No. 6)) Bill 2014

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would adapt six appropriation Acts to the Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act, replacing references to the Commonwealth's previous financial management legislation.
It would update how agencies, corporate bodies, accountable authorities and special accounts are identified, while recognising transitional rules that preserve parts of the older framework.

The changes would cover specified non-ordinary-service appropriation Acts for 2012-2013, 2013-2014 and 2014-2015, with commencement coordinated with the new framework and relevant appropriation legislation.
changes: General drawing rights limits would be treated as debit limits from 1 July 2015.
Notes requiring drawing rights before appropriations can be used would be removed.
The latest appropriation would expressly allow corporate bodies' funds to be paid directly from the Consolidated Revenue Fund.
References governing notional payments would be updated.
summary.affected: Commonwealth entities, Commonwealth companies and their accountable authorities would be affected.

divisions.question: Brendan O'Connor I move the opposition amendment to the Public Governance, Performance and Accountability (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2014, as circulated under my name: (1) Schedule 2, page 28 (after line 15), after item 58, insert: 58A Guidelines The amendments to section 65 of the FMA Act made by this Schedule do not affect the continuity of the Commonwealth Cleaning Services Guidelines 2012, as in force immediately before the commencement time. As I said earlier in my contribution to the debate on these bills, the opposition has grave concerns about the impact of the Commonwealth Cleaning Services Guidelines and their potential impact upon cleaners' rates of pay going forward. In this place we had the Prime Minister, when questions were put to him on this matter during question time, give an unqualified guarantee that cleaners who work under Commonwealth contracts would not lose any payment or suffer any loss to or reductions of their hourly rate of pay. If this amendment is not supported by the government, those unqualified statements will be found to be untrue. The only issue is whether the Prime Minister intentionally misled this parliament by answering as he did the questions asked of him about the impact on cleaners under Commonwealth contracts. As the member for Watson and the member for Bendigo have said in this debate, the repeal of this guideline will mean that, when future contracts are tendered, those tendering will be able—if they are successful—to reduce the rates of pay for cleaners under that contract by almost $5 an hour. That is what would happen to cleaners as a result of the provision contained within this bill. For that reason, and so that we can ensure that the Prime Minister did not mislead this place in question time when asked about this matter, we would expect the government to support this amendment. speeches.speaker: Michael McCormack
speeches.brief: Introduced the third bill in the package, covering Appropriation Acts (No. 2), (No. 4) and (No. 6), to modify terminology for amounts other than the ordinary annual services of government.

speeches.speaker: Christopher Pyne
speeches.brief: Moved a debate management motion to fast-track the Public Governance, Performance and Accountability bills and related appropriation bills through the House before the end of the financial year, noting the usual longer period for consideration had not been possible this time.
